mission.title: security-compliance: [Bug]: Failed to use openid.oidc with bearer.oidc authorization being configured
mission.description: [Bug]: Failed to use openid.oidc with bearer.oidc authorization being configured. Requested by 6+ users.

steps.title: Check current security-compliance deployment
steps.description:
Verify your security-compliance version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/name=security-compliance
helm list -n security-compliance 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working security-compliance installation.

steps.title: Review security-compliance configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant security-compliance configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/name=security-compliance
kubectl get configmap -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=security-compliance
```
### zot version

2.1.16

### Describe the bug

I configured openid authorization via Vault OIDC and it was working until I have added Workload OIDC authorization via bearer.oidc.
Sign in with Vault stopped to work with 400 error.

steps.title: Apply the fix for [Bug]: Failed to use openid.oidc with bearer.oidc…
steps.description:
# Registry Client Authentication Flows — Study for Auth Redesign

Scope: client-side (tool) behavior only — how the OCI clients zot integrates with
decide *whether* to authenticate and *which* scheme (Basic vs Bearer/token) to use.

Related issues / PRs:

-
```yaml
http:
  auth:
    apikey: true
    htpasswd:
      path: /run/registry/htpasswd
    bearer:
      realm: zot
      service: zot
      oidc:
        - issuer: https://kube.mydomain:6443
          audiences:
            - https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local
          claimMapping:
            username: claims.sub
    openid:
      providers:
        oidc:
          name: Vault
          issuer: https://vault.mydomain/v1/identity/oidc/provider/zot
          credentialsfile: /run/registry/oidc_creds.json
          claimMapping: { username: username }
          scopes: [openid, user]
```

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/name=security-compliance
kubectl get events -n security-compliance --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "[Bug]: Failed to use openid.oidc with bearer.oidc…" is functioning correctly.
